landing.onboardingBanner: GIIPS is an AI-assisted triage layer designed to work alongside official Tamil Nadu grievance systems — it is a hackathon prototype demonstrating automated complaint clustering and prioritization, not a replacement for government portals.
landing.problemTitle: Municipal staff are overwhelmed by complaint volume
landing.problemBody: Citizens report the same issues repeatedly. Officers manually read and triage each one, with no way to automatically detect duplicates or prioritize urgent cases. Critical problems get buried, and response times suffer.
landing.solutionTitle: An AI triage layer for existing grievance workflows
landing.solutionBody: GIIPS automatically classifies incoming complaints, merges duplicates into a single incident, and assigns a priority score — so officers review fewer, more actionable items. It is designed as a supplemental triage layer, not a replacement for official government portals.
landing.impactBody: In a benchmark against 10,000 synthetic complaints, GIIPS collapsed them into 160 actionable incident clusters — reducing officer triage volume by 98.4%. Estimated time saved: <0>~1,666 officer-hours</0>.
landing.impactCaveat: These figures are based on synthetic complaint data (not live grievance records) using an SBERT-based clustering model. Real-world free-text data with greater linguistic variety would likely yield a lower reduction rate, bounded below by an alternative TF-IDF estimate of ~50%. The metric is a validated upper bound, not a production guarantee.

header.title: Methodology
header.subtitle: How GIIPS processes complaints into actionable intelligence

intro.title: From 100 Complaints to 15 Actionable Incidents
intro.body: GIIPS uses natural language processing and clustering algorithms to collapse hundreds of individual complaints into a small set of actionable incident clusters — dramatically reducing the triage burden on officers.

pipeline.title: AI Processing Pipeline
pipeline.stage1Desc: Complaints are submitted via the web portal and prepared for analysis. Text is cleaned and converted to TF-IDF vector representations for classification.
pipeline.stage2Desc: Each complaint is classified into a civic category using a trained TF-IDF + Logistic Regression model, with keyword-based fallback for Tamil text. Related complaints are grouped using text similarity.
pipeline.stage2Items: TF-IDF Vectors, Logistic Regression, Text Similarity
pipeline.stage3Desc: Each cluster receives a priority score based on severity keywords, complaint volume, geographic spread, and escalation patterns. Priority rules are applied to flag critical incidents.
pipeline.stage3Items: Severity Analysis, Volume Weighting, Rule Engine
pipeline.stage4Desc: Final incident records are created with linked complaints, priority scores, and recommended actions. Results are displayed on the dashboard and trigger in-app notifications to relevant officers.

architecture.title: System Architecture
architecture.subtitle: End-to-end data flow and component overview
architecture.noteBody: This is a hackathon prototype. The web portal is the only active data source. In-app notifications are database-stored (no email/SMS). The AI engine runs a trained scikit-learn model with keyword-based fallbacks. A message queue, API gateway, mobile app, and call center are not yet implemented.

metrics.title: Performance Metrics
metrics.caveat: Measured on synthetic training data — not yet validated on real citizen complaints
metrics.accuracyDesc: Overall classification accuracy across all complaint categories.
metrics.precisionDesc: Proportion of correctly identified duplicates among all flagged duplicates.
metrics.recallDesc: Proportion of actual duplicates successfully detected by the system.
metrics.f1ScoreDesc: Harmonic mean of precision and recall, balancing both metrics.

helpWidget.title: Help & FAQ
helpWidget.q1: How do I track my complaint?
helpWidget.a1: Enter your complaint ID on the Track Complaint page, or view it under My Complaints after logging in.
helpWidget.a2: Your complaint has been marked resolved. You need to verify the resolution using the 6-digit code from your notifications to close it.
helpWidget.q3: How do I reopen a resolved complaint?
helpWidget.a3: Open the complaint detail page and click Reopen if you are not satisfied with the resolution.
helpWidget.q4: How do I submit a complaint?
helpWidget.a4: Log in and go to Citizen Portal. Fill in the details, location, add an optional photo, and submit. Our AI processes it automatically.
helpWidget.q5: How do I rate a resolved complaint?
helpWidget.a5: After verifying the resolution, you can rate it using the star rating on the complaint detail page.
helpWidget.a6: Our AI classifies, groups related complaints, and assigns a priority. You receive a tracking ID and status updates via notifications.
